verdicts.factCheck: Directory.Packages.props at tag 2.3.0-rc pins Nethermind.Numerics.Int256 1.15.0 (line 70) and at tag 2.2.2 pins 1.11.0 (line 69). src/Nethermind/Directory.Build.props at 2.3.0-rc gives VersionPrefix 2.3.0 and VersionSuffix rc. The NuGet registration index lists 1.11.0 published 2026-10-06T21:57Z and 1.15.0 published 2026-11-16T17:51Z, with 1.12.0, 1.13.0 and 1.14.0 between them. clientdiversity.org shows Nethermind at 25.46 percent in one source and 43 percent in another. In Int256 v1.15.0, UInt256.divmod.cs MultiplyMod sends a modulus of 2^256 - 1 to the fold in MultiplyModWideCore (lines 367-404) before any other reduction, and the fold is correct: lo + hi with a carry adds one, which cannot overflow because lo + hi - 2^256 is at most 2^256 - 2, and an all ones result maps to zero. UInt256.std.cs Remainder512ByFullModulus (lines 399-412) takes Remainder512ByKnownModulus only when hi.u2 or hi.u3 is nonzero, that is a product of at least 2^384, and the modulus top limb equals one of five named constants; otherwise it calls Remainder512By256Bits. In Remainder512By256Bits (divmod.cs lines 2507-2571) the new test drops the leading quotient digit when the top nonzero dividend limb t is below d3. I checked the shifted arm by hand: t < d3 < 2^(64 - shift) keeps the extra limb w8 at zero, and the normalised top limb is at most ((d3 - 1) << shift) + 2^shift - 1, which is below d3 << shift and so below nd3, so the skipped digit is zero. The shift of zero arm is the same test with the extra limb already zero. The test is strict. A read-only eth_call against https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com (reth/v2.11.0-b9abbcc) with a state override running mulmod on 60 cases, moduli 2^256 - 1, random four limb values and operands at the 2^224 by 2^160 shape and near 2^256, gave 0 mismatches against Python. I could not open the GitHub release page for 2.3.0-rc from this session, so the 2026-11-23 publication date and the pre-release label rest on the research file alone. The tag and its version files exist.
verdicts.codeCheck: Every MULMOD in src is at src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24 (modulus not(0)), FullMath.sol:48 and :112 (modulus the caller's denominator) and src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:252 (modulus Q96). src has no addmod. I listed every mulDiv caller with grep and bounded each product. Position.sol:94 and :96 multiply a 256 bit difference by a uint128 liquidity, so the product is below 2^384. SqrtPriceMath.sol:47 and :71 multiply numerator1 = liquidity << 96, below 2^224, by a uint160 price. SqrtPriceMath.sol:97 and :105 multiply an amount by 2^96. SqrtPriceMath.sol:208-209 multiply numerator1 by a price difference below 2^160. SqrtPriceMath.sol:250-252 multiply a uint128 by a value below 2^160. SwapMath.sol:65, :74 and :104 multiply by at most 10^6. Pool.sol:403 and :472 use plain arithmetic, not mulDiv. No product other than the one at FullMath.sol:24 reaches 2^384, so the Barrett and known modulus paths cannot run from src, and FullMath.sol:24 takes the fold. The denominator at SqrtPriceMath.sol:44-47 can be any four limb value, so the 4 limb remainder routine with the new leading digit test is reached there, as the finding says. A wrong result would show up in the require at FullMath.sol:30 and in the quotient. That would make one client compute a different post-state, which is a consensus split and not a transfer of value.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Whether the new Barrett and pseudo-Mersenne paths of Int256 1.15.0 can be reached from any MULMOD in src.
clearedSpotChecks.note: UInt256.std.cs:399-412 requires hi.u2 or hi.u3 nonzero, a product of at least 2^384, and a top limb equal to one of five constants. My own grep of src lists every mulmod and mulDiv caller; the only product above 2^384 is at FullMath.sol:24, whose modulus 2^256 - 1 is taken by the fold at divmod.cs:379 first. Every other product is below 2^384 by the operand widths at Position.sol:94-96, SqrtPriceMath.sol:47, 71, 97, 105, 208-209, 250-252 and SwapMath.sol:65, 74, 104.

clearedSpotChecks.check: The leading quotient digit test that Int256 1.15.0 added to Remainder512By256Bits and Remainder512By192Bits, the 4 limb remainder MULMOD reaches at SqrtPriceMath.sol:44-47.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I read divmod.cs:2507-2571 and checked both arms by hand. With t the top nonzero limb and t < d3, the shifted extra limb is t >> (64 - shift), which is zero because d3 < 2^(64 - shift), and the normalised top limb is below nd3, so the skipped digit is zero and no dividend limb is lost. The 192 bit variant at line 2340 has the same shape with d2; I did not trace it as far.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Nethermind's fused PUSH2 with JUMP or JUMPI in untraced execution, against the unfused sequence, at 2.2.2 and 2.3.0-rc.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I read InstructionPush2Core in EvmInstructions.Stack.cs at 2.3.0-rc. It charges 3 for the push, checks the stack limit before fusing, reads the two byte destination big endian, charges JUMP or JUMPI gas, pops the condition with a depth check, falls through without validating on a zero condition, validates the destination on a taken jump, and charges JUMPDEST gas for the landed byte. With lazy analysis and an unanalysed destination it runs unfused. The next byte after a PUSH2 immediate is always an instruction boundary, so the fusion cannot pick up a data byte. I found no difference in stack, gas, program counter or outcome. I did not read the 2.2.2 text.
